questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mostly the city, country, climate and surrounding nature. Academics came in second priority.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: University of Sydney was very good at taking care of exchange students and providing information of what to do, when and where to show up, deadlines etc. That made it really easy, you were really taken by the had all the way through.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mail correspondances and students that showed us around on the welcome day

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Student accommodations (collegium)
Shared apartments

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: communal kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If choosing Collegium (Queen Mary building) you need to buy every utensils at arrival

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the rooms was not too big, half of them have a view directly into a parking lot, you cannot hang anything on the walls, communal toilets and kitchen. It was nice to have your own fridge in the room though. The social life definitely made the housing better.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online portal was super easy and straightforward to use

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Exchange supervisor takes you through every step of the way via mail + information sheets

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful - I got all the classes I wanted. And it was easy to change classes as well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it before deadline for better classes

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3000 and 4000 level classes

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar with lectures, workshops and laboratory classes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Medical and Applied Virology
Pathogenesis 
Immunology in Human Disease 
Learning i Outdoor Education

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Learning in Outdoor Education - why? 
- Doesn't require a lot, only write a few blog posts
- No exam
- Only other exchange students 
- Go on field trips to see Australian Nature

Medical and Applied virology/Immunogy in human disease - why?
- Very well structured courses
- Overlapping lectures
- Super interesting content

questions.answer: All kitchen stuff, duvets, pillows, unexpected fees (e.g. exit cleaning fee)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Coffee is very cheap
Capsicums and cucumber are insanely expensive 
Otherwise everything else is similar to danish prices

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were sooo many societies and clubs you could become a member of (chocolate, asian muscicians, surfing, quidditch etc)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I played spike ball, which was super fun 
Surfsociety have som pretty nice events like boat party in the harbour

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
GO ON TRIPS
rent a car to see nearby areas like Palm beach, Mermaid pools, Cronulla beach, Figure 8 pools, Blue mountains. Or fly to Uluru, Melbourne, Brisbane.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, somehow similar to western danish culture. The city is not as cozy as copenhagen

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to speak with an australian accents, always a conversation starter. Go to clubs or bars to met some locals. Talk to locals in lab classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The australian hospitalily and accent (How are ya going? cheers mate)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prioritize place over academics
2. You will get homesick
3. Go on adventure, explore the local areas

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life - all the new friends I've made and all the cool places I've seen. You really get pushed out of your comfort zone sometimes, which made you develop as a person.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To not spend too much money.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO ON EXCHANGE

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
